about: Case file CF6 (cf6-shifting-load-to-clean-hours). Research text: the text of the study step of the timeline, 'boundary' (its lists) and each fact's 'what' are approved excerpt sentences (E6, with their revisions after review), word for word; _tests/learn/test_cf6-shifting-load-to-clean-hours.js checks them. The paper's date is the publisher's date on Crossref (accessed 3 Nov 2026). 'idea' uses Prairie Town (fictional; plants, sizes and CO2 rates illustrative, from town.json) on the real shapes of 9 June 2025 on the Southwest Power Pool grid (EIA-930, town_year.json), the day lesson 9 uses, scaled the same way. Each hour is dispatched cheapest first as in lesson 9 (no ramp limits, no minimum output): the town's 100 MW zero-carbon plant runs flat, then wind and sun, then the combined-cycle plant, then the peaker; a negative gap is spilled wind and sun.

events.label: Journal article (this case)
events.text: Load re-timed by hourly average emission intensity in U.S. grid regions, with windows of a month, a quarter or a year.

source.label: Li et al. (2025), Cell Reports Sustainability 2, 100367

boundary.title: Where the result holds
holds: emissions are counted at each hour's [[average-emission-factor|average]] intensity;
each window is known in advance (perfect foresight);
each window's total use does not fall;
hourly EIA data for U.S. grid regions in 2023.
leaves: the grid's consequential response: which plants actually change output (the [[marginal-emission-factor|marginal]] view);
the cost of moving load, apart from a penalty on each adjusted hour.
boundary.source: From Li et al. (2025), Cell Reports Sustainability.

idea.title: Move 10 MWh in Prairie Town's day
idea.note: Prairie Town is illustrative: its plants and CO₂ rates are invented; the hourly shapes are real (9 June 2025, Southwest Power Pool).
how: Negative means less CO₂; t means metric tonnes.
The dashed line is the factor for the next MWh. A 10 MWh move can cross from one plant to the next, so the readouts work out each plant's output again in both hours.
The toy moves energy freely between hours; real loads have deadlines, comfort limits and storage losses.
terms: The [[marginal-plant|plant on the margin]] serves the next MWh: the [[combined-cycle|combined-cycle plant]], the [[peaker|peaker]], or spare wind and sun.
Spare wind and sun would otherwise be [[curtailment|spilled]]: available, but not used.

facts.what: In grids with diverse generation resources, expanding the adjustment range from ±5% to ±8% can boost carbon reductions from 1.19% to 1.64%.
facts.source: Li et al. (2025), Cell Reports Sustainability

facts.n: one to two percent or less
facts.what: In the reported scenarios, reductions in attributed emissions were on the order of one to two percent of regional totals or less.
facts.source: Li et al. (2025), Cell Reports Sustainability
